study_id: Liou et al. - 2025 - Survival machine learning methods for mortality prediction after heart transplantation in the contem

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study analyzes adult heart transplant recipients using machine learning survival algorithms (non‑linear models) to predict one‑year mortality, published in a peer‑reviewed journal after 2018, meeting all inclusion criteria.

identification_methods.Setting: National registry (Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients) study
identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective benchmark study using SRTR data to evaluate survival ML methods for heart transplantation mortality.
identification_methods.Institution: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included adult (≥18 years) heart-only transplant recipients receiving first transplant; excluded multi-organ transplants and those <18 years.
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: Lasso, Ridge, Elastic Net (penalized Cox), Cox Gradient Boost, XGBoost Linear, XGBoost Tree, Random Survival Forests
identification_methods.Input Variables: 75 demographic, clinical, recipient, waitlist, donor and procedural variables (114 after one‑hot encoding)
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Multiple imputation with chained equations (MICE) for variables <20% missing; excluded >20% missingness
identification_methods.Validation Method: Nested 5‑repeat, 5‑fold cross‑validation with 90/10 train‑holdout split; hyperparameter tuning via random search (25 iterations); external validation on seasonally matched pre‑policy cohort
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Data standardized (z‑score), one‑hot encoded; models built using mlr package in R; Bonferroni adjustment applied to p‑values; code available on GitHub

population.Inclusion criteria: Adult heart-only transplant recipients who received their first transplant on or after October 18, 2018
population.Exclusion criteria: Recipients <18 years of age at transplant and multi-organ transplants
population.Population Notes: Post-policy cohort of 7,160 adult heart-only transplant recipients with at least one recorded follow-up; also a seasonally-matched pre-policy cohort used for comparison
population.Diagnosis: Various cardiac etiologies; most common idiopathic (37.7%)
population.Diagnosis Overall: Various cardiac etiologies; most common idiopathic (37.7%)

interventions_outcomes.Specific Algorithm Name: Lasso, Ridge, Elastic Net, Cox Gradient Boost, XGBoost Linear, XGBoost Tree, Random Survival Forests
interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: SRTR registry data (demographic, clinical, recipient, waitlist, donor, procedural variables)
interventions_outcomes.Feature Selection Method: Multiple imputation, z-score standardization, one‑hot encoding; no pre‑selection before model training
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Time-to-event survival analysis with censoring at 1 year
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Nested 5‑repeat, 5‑fold cross‑validation; random search hyperparameter tuning; models trained on training set and evaluated on holdout set
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: Holdout C‑indices reported for each model; best was Random Survival Forests (C‑index 0.628)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reporting: C-index 0.628 for Random Survival Forests (best model)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: Proportion of concordant pairs in survival predictions (Harrell's C‑index)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: Machine learning models provided reasonable prediction of 1‑year mortality but were not statistically superior to Cox model
